# Ordinal Numbers (서수) - Korean Perspective

한국인이 한국어 서수 어휘를 학습할 때 + 일본어 번역 비교. 10 entries (첫째~열째) 와 한자어 비교.

## 서수 (Ordinal Numbers)

| 한국어 | 일어 | 일어 IPA |
|---|---|---|
| 첫째 (cheotjjae) | 一番目 (いちばんめ, ichibanme) | /i.tɕi.baɴ.me/ |
| 둘째 (duljjae) | 二番目 (にばんめ, nibanme) | /ni.baɴ.me/ |
| 셋째 (setjjae) | 三番目 (さんばんめ, sanbanme) | /sam.baɴ.me/ |
| 넷째 (netjjae) | 四番目 (よんばんめ, yonbanme) | /jon.baɴ.me/ |
| 다섯째 (daseotjjae) | 五番目 (ごばんめ, gobanme) | /ɡo.baɴ.me/ |
| 여섯째 (yeoseotjjae) | 六番目 (ろくばんめ, rokubanme) | /ɾo.kɯ.baɴ.me/ |
| 일곱째 (ilgopjjae) | 七番目 (ななばんめ, nanabanme) | /na.na.baɴ.me/ |
| 여덟째 (yeodeoljjae) | 八番目 (はちばんめ, hachibanme) | /ha.tɕi.baɴ.me/ |
| 아홉째 (ahopjjae) | 九番目 (くばんめ, kubanme) | /kɯ.baɴ.me/ |
| 열째 (yeoljjae) | 十番目 (じゅうばんめ, jūbanme) | /dʑɯː.baɴ.me/ |

## 한국어 학습 노트

**한국어 서수 = 순 우리말 + 접미사 '째' (째)**: 첫째 (첫 + 짜) / 둘째 (둘 + 짜) 등. **일어 서수 = 한자어 + 접미사 '目 (め)'**: 一番目 (いち + ばん + め) / 二番目 (に + ばん + め) 등. **韓 서수 접미사 '째' (chae)** = **日 서수 접미사 '目 (め, me)** 어원 비교.

# 직업 어휘 (Korean Career/Workplace)

**Source:** [[career-vocabulary]]
**Theme:** 직업/직장
**Level:** TOPIK 3-4 / B1-B2

한국어 직업 어휘: 직업/직함, 직장/회사, 사무/회의/이메일, 직장 위계, 구직/이력서. 출처: TOPIK N4-N5, 국립국어원, 고용노동부.

---

## 직업/직함

### 의사

**품사:** 명사

**정의:** 환자를 진료하는 의료 전문가.

**로마자:** uisa

**한자:** 醫師

#### 예문

- **의사**가 진료를 합니다. — 의료
- 저는 **의사**입니다. — 자기소개

#### 관련어

- ''간호사'' — nurse
- ''병원'' — hospital

#### 출처

- [[career-vocabulary]]
- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 변호사

**품사:** 명사

**정의:** 법률 자문을 제공하고 소송을 대리하는 전문가.

**로마자:** byeonhosa

**한자:** �護士

#### 예문

- **변호사**에게 상담합니다. — 법률
- **변호사**가 소송을 담당합니다. — 재판

#### 출처

- [[career-vocabulary]]
- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 엔지니어

**품사:** 명사

**정의:** 기술적 문제를 해결하는 전문가.

**로마자:** enjinieo

#### 예문

- **엔지니어**가 설계를 합니다. — 기술
- 소프트웨어 **엔지니어**로 일합니다. — 직업

#### 출처

- [[career-vocabulary]]

---

### 교사

**품사:** 명사

**정의:** 학교에서 학생을 가르치는 사람.

**로마자:** gyosa

**한자:** 教師

#### 예문

- **교사**가 수업을 합니다. — 교육
- 저는 **교사**입니다. — 자기소개

#### 관련어

- ''선생님'' — honorific teacher
- ''학교'' — school

#### 출처

- [[career-vocabulary]]

---

### 매니저

**품사:** 명사

**정의:** 팀이나 부서를 관리하는 사람.

**로마자:** maenijeo

#### 예문

- **매니저**가 팀을 이끕니다. — 관리
- 프로젝트 **매니저**로 일합니다. — 업무

#### 관련어

- ''팀장'' — team leader
- ''부장'' — department head

- [[career-vocabulary]]

- ''사무실'' — office

# body-vocabulary — Body Parts

**Source:** Oxford 3000 (CEFR A1-A2) + OEC frequency list
**Theme:** body-vocabulary
**Level:** A1-A2

Essential body part vocabulary for beginner English learners. Sourced from Oxford 3000 word list (CEFR A1-A2) and the Oxford English Corpus (OEC) frequency rankings. Each entry is foundational vocabulary for describing health, appearance, and physical sensation.

---

## Head & Face

### head

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the upper part of the body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /hɛd/

**Etymology:** Old English "heafod", from Proto-Germanic *haubudą. Cognate with German "Haupt".

#### Examples

- My head hurts. — 머리가 아파요.
- She nodded her head. — 그녀가 고개를 끄덕였다.

#### Related Terms

- ''brain''
- ''skull''
- ''forehead''

#### Cultural Notes

In English, "head" is metonymically used for "mind" or "intelligence" (e.g., "use your head", "a head for heights"). In Korean translations, this is often rendered as "머리" but the English idiom may map better to "머리를 써" (use your brain).

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### face

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the front part of a person's head, from forehead to chin

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /feɪs/

**Etymology:** From Old French "face", from Latin "facies" (form, appearance, face).

#### Examples

- She has a round face. — 그녀는 둥근 얼굴을 가졌다.
- Wash your face. — 얼굴을 씻어.

#### Related Terms

- ''forehead''
- ''cheek''
- ''chin''
- ''jaw''

#### Cultural Notes

In English idioms, "face" carries strong social meaning: "lose face" (체면 잃다), "save face" (체면을 살리다), "face-to-face" (직접, 대면으로). These are loan translations of East Asian concepts into English.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### eye

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of a pair of globular organs of sight in the head

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /aɪ/

**Etymology:** Old English "ēage", from Proto-Germanic *augō. Cognate with German "Auge".

#### Examples

- She has blue eyes. — 그녀는 파란 눈을 가졌다.
- Keep your eyes open. — 눈을 뜨고 있어.

#### Related Terms

- ''eyebrow''
- ''eyelash''
- ''pupil''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### ear

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the organ of hearing and balance in humans and other vertebrates

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɪər/

**Etymology:** Old English "ēare", from Proto-Germanic *auzō. Cognate with German "Ohr".

#### Examples

- I have an ear infection. — 귀가 감염됐다.
- She has good ears for music. — 그녀는 음악에 귀가 밝다.

#### Related Terms

- ''eardrum''
- ''hearing''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### nose

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the part of the face above the mouth, containing the nostrils and used for breathing and smelling

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /noʊz/

**Etymology:** Old English "nosu", from Proto-Germanic *nusō. Cognate with German "Nase".

#### Examples

- He has a big nose. — 그는 코가 크다.
- She blew her nose. — 그녀는 코를 풀었다.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### mouth

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the opening in the human or animal face through which food is taken and from which sounds are emitted

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /maʊθ/

**Etymology:** Old English "mūth", from Proto-Germanic *munthaz. Cognate with German "Mund".

#### Examples

- Open your mouth. — 입을 열어.
- She covered her mouth. — 그녀는 입을 막았다.

#### Related Terms

- ''lip''
- ''tongue''
- ''tooth''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Torso

### chest

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the front surface of the upper body, from the neck to the abdomen

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /tʃɛst/

**Etymology:** Old English "cest" (box, coffin), from Proto-Germanic *kistō. Original meaning was "container"; modern anatomical sense from 16th c. Distinguish from "breast" (가슴, mammary).

#### Examples

- He has a broad chest. — 그는 가슴이 넓다.
- She has a pain in her chest. — 그녀는 가슴이 아프다.

#### Related Terms

- ''breast''
- ''rib''
- ''heart''

#### Cultural Notes

Korean "가슴" can mean both "chest" and "breast" — English distinguishes. For health/anatomy, prefer "chest". For mammary context, "breast". For emotional context (e.g., "가슴이 아프다"), "heart" or "chest" both work.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### back

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the hips

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /bæk/

**Etymology:** Old English "bæc", from Proto-Germanic *baką. Cognate with German "Bach" (back, brook — different semantic shift).

#### Examples

- My back hurts. — 등이 아파요.
- She carried the baby on her back. — 그녀는 아기를 등에 업었다.

#### Related Terms

- ''spine''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### stomach

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the internal organ in which the first part of digestion occurs

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈstʌmək/

**Etymology:** From Latin "stomachus", from Greek "stomakhos" (gullet), from "stoma" (mouth). Spelling influenced by Latin.

#### Examples

- I have a stomach ache. — 배가 아파요.
- My stomach is full. — 배가 부르다.

#### Related Terms

- ''belly'' (informal)
- ''abdomen''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Limbs

### arm

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the two upper limbs of the human body from the shoulder to the hand

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɑːrm/

**Etymology:** Old English "arm", from Proto-Germanic *armaz. Cognate with German "Arm".

#### Examples

- She broke her arm. — 그녀는 팔을 부러뜨렸다.
- He carried the box under his arm. — 그는 팔 밑에 상자를 들고 갔다.

#### Related Terms

- ''elbow''
- ''wrist''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### hand

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the end of the human arm beyond the wrist, including the palm, fingers, and thumb

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /hænd/

**Etymology:** Old English "hand", from Proto-Germanic *handuz. Cognate with German "Hand".

#### Examples

- Wash your hands. — 손을 씻어.
- Give me a hand. — 도와줘.

#### Related Terms

- ''finger''
- ''palm''
- ''thumb''
- ''nail''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### leg

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the limbs on which a person or animal walks

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /lɛɡ/

**Etymology:** From Old Norse "leggr" (leg, limb). Replaced Old English "shank".

#### Examples

- She hurt her leg. — 그녀는 다리를 다쳤다.
- He crossed his legs. — 그는 다리를 꼬았다.

#### Related Terms

- ''knee''
- ''ankle''
- ''foot''
- ''thigh''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### foot

**Part of Speech:** noun (plural: feet)

**Definition:** the lower extremity of the leg below the ankle, on which a person stands or walks

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /fʊt/ (plural: /fiːt/)

**Etymology:** Old English "fōt", from Proto-Germanic *fōts. Cognate with German "Fuß".

#### Examples

- I hurt my foot. — 발을 다쳤어요.
- She stood on one foot. — 그녀는 한 발로 섰다.

#### Related Terms

- ''toe''
- ''heel''
- ''ankle''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Other Essentials

### finger

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the four slender jointed parts attached to either hand

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈfɪŋɡər/

**Etymology:** Old English "finger", from Proto-Germanic *fingraz. Cognate with German "Finger".

#### Examples

- She pointed her finger. — 그녀는 손가락으로 가리켰다.
- I cut my finger. — 손가락을 베었어요.

#### Related Terms

- ''thumb''
- ''index finger''
- ''nail''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### neck

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the part of a person's body connecting the head to the rest of the body

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /nɛk/

**Etymology:** Old English "hnecca" (back of neck), from Proto-Germanic *hnekk-. Cognate with German "Nacken".

#### Examples

- My neck is stiff. — 목이 뻣뻣해요.
- She wore a necklace around her neck. — 그녀는 목에 목걸이를 했다.

#### Related Terms

- ''throat''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

# months vocabulary - 달(月) 어휘 (Korean Translation)

**Overview:** 영어 월(月) 어휘의 한국어 번역본. 일상 대화 및 날짜 표현에 자주 사용되는 필수 단어 모음.

### January (1월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 1월 — 양력 첫 번째 달. 한국어 한자어 "일월(一月)" 또는 "정월(正月)" (음력 첫 달) / "1월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈdʒæn.ju.ɛr.i/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "Januarie", 라틴어 "Januarius" (Janus, 시작의 신). 한국어 한자어 "정월(正月)"은 음력 첫 달 의미, 양력은 "1월".

#### Examples

- **January** is the first month. — 1월은 첫 번째 달이에요.
- New Year's Day is in **January**. — 새해 첫 날은 1월이에요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- New Year (새해)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "January" 발음: /ˈdʒæn.ju.ɛr.i/. 한국어 1월은 양력 기준. 한국 전통 설날은 음력 1월 (보통 1-2월 양력). 영어 "January" 라틴 신 Janus에서 유래 (두 얼굴 = 과거/미래).

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### February (2월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 2월 — 양력 두 번째 달. 한국어 "이월(二月)" / "2월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈfɛb.ru.ɛr.i/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "Februarie", 라틴어 "Februarius" (Februa, 정화의 축제). 한국어 한자어 "이월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **February** has 28 days. — 2월은 28일까지 있어요.
- **February** is the shortest month. — 2월은 가장 짧은 달이에요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- leap year (윤년)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "February" 발음: /ˈfɛb.ru.ɛr.i/. 한국어 학습자에게 발음 주의 ("Feb-ruary" 끊지 말고). 영어 "February" 28일 / 29일 (윤년). 한국 음력 2월 = 정월 다음 달, 음력 1-2월 = 설 연휴.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### March (3월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 3월 — 양력 세 번째 달. 한국어 "삼월(三月)" / "3월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /mɑːrtʃ/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "March", 라틴어 "Martius" (Mars, 전쟁의 신). 한국어 한자어 "삼월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **March** is the third month. — 3월은 세 번째 달이에요.
- Spring begins in **March**. — 봄은 3월에 시작돼요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- spring (봄)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "March" 발음: /mɑːrtʃ/ (tch 발음, 한국어에 없음). 한국어 학습자에게 "March" 발음 주의. 한국에서 3월 = 봄 시작, 새학기. 영어 "in like a lion, out like a lamb" = 3월 시작은 거칠고 끝은 온화.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### April (4월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 4월 — 양력 네 번째 달. 한국어 "사월(四月)" / "4월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈeɪ.pɚl/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "April", 라틴어 "Aprilis" (Aphrodite, 사랑의 신). 한국어 한자어 "사월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **April** has 30 days. — 4월은 30일까지 있어요.
- Spring flowers bloom in **April**. — 4월에 봄꽃이 피어요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- April Fools' Day (만우절)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "April" 발음: /ˈeɪ.pɚl/. 한국어 학습자에게 발음 주의. 한국 4월 = 벚꽃, 학기 시작. 영어 "April showers bring May flowers" = 4월 비가 5월 꽃을 피게 한다.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### May (5월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 5월 — 양력 다섯 번째 달. 한국어 "오월(五月)" / "5월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /meɪ/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "Maius", 라틴어 "Maius mensis" (Maia, 봄의 신). 한국어 한자어 "오월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **May** is the fifth month. — 5월은 다섯 번째 달이에요.
- Children's Day is in **May**. — 어린이날은 5월이에요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- spring (봄)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "May" 발음: /meɪ/. 한국어 5월 = 가정의 달 (어버이날 5/8, 성년의 날, 부부의 날). 영어 "may"는 일반 동사 (허락하다)와 동일 발음. 한국어 학습자 주의 — 5월 + May 발음 연습.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### June (6월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 6월 — 양력 여섯 번째 달. 한국어 "유월(六月)" / "6월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /dʒuːn/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "June", 라틴어 "Junius" (Juno, 결혼의 신). 한국어 한자어 "유월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **June** is the sixth month. — 6월은 여섯 번째 달이에요.
- **June** has the longest day. — 6월은 하루가 가장 길어요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- summer (여름)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "June" 발음: /dʒuːn/ (긴 모음). 한국어 6월 = 초여름, 장마 시작 (한국 장마 보통 6월 말~7월 중순). 영어 "June bride" = 6월 결혼 (전통적 행복).

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### July (7월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 7월 — 양력 일곱 번째 달. 한국어 "칠월(七月)" / "7월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /dʒʊˈlaɪ/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "Julie", 라틴어 "Julius" (Julius Caesar, 로마 정치가). 한국어 한자어 "칠월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **July** is very hot. — 7월은 매우 더워요.
- I was born in **July**. — 나는 7월에 태어났어요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- summer vacation (여름 휴가)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "July" 발음: /dʒʊˈlaɪ/. 한국어 7월 = 한여름, 한국 학생 여름방학 시작. 영어 "Independence Day" (미국, 7/4) = "July 4th". 한국 광복절 8/15와 다름.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### August (8월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 8월 — 양력 여덟 번째 달. 한국어 "팔월(八月)" / "8월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈɔː.ɡəst/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "August", 라틴어 "Augustus" (Augustus Caesar, 첫 로마 황제). 한국어 한자어 "팔월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **August** is summer vacation. — 8월은 여름방학이에요.
- **August** is very hot in Korea. — 한국에서 8월은 매우 더워요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- summer (여름)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "August" 발음: /ˈɔː.ɡəst/. 한국어 8월 = 한여름, 광복절 (8/15). 영어 "August" 발음 주의 — 첫 모음 /ɔː/ (한국어 "어"에 가까움). 영어 관용 표현: "August vacation".

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### September (9월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 9월 — 양력 아홉 번째 달. 한국어 "구월(九月)" / "9월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /sɛpˈtɛm.bər/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "September", 라틴어 "September" (septem, 7 → 원래 로마력 7월). 한국어 한자어 "구월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **September** is autumn. — 9월은 가을이에요.
- School starts in **September**. — 9월에 학교가 시작돼요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- fall (가을, 미국)
- autumn (가을, 영국)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "September" 발음: /sɛpˈtɛm.bər/. 한국어 9월 = 가을 시작, 개학/학년 시작. 영어 "September"는 원래 로마력 7월 (septem = 7), 율리우스력 추가 후 9월 이동.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

### October (10월)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (noun)

**Definition:** 10월 — 양력 열 번째 달. 한국어 "시월(十月)" / "10월".

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɑːkˈtoʊ.bər/

**Etymology:** 중세 영어 "October", 라틴어 "October" (octo, 8 → 원래 로마력 8월). 한국어 한자어 "시월"은 한자.

#### Examples

- **October** has Halloween. — 10월에는 할로윈이 있어요.
- Leaves change color in **October**. — 10월에 나뭇잎이 색이 변해요.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[months-vocabulary]]
- Halloween (할로윈)

#### Cultural Notes

영어 "October" 발음: /ɑːkˈtoʊ.bər/. 한국어 10월 = 가을, 한글날 (10/9). 영어 "October"는 원래 로마력 8월. 한국에서 "10월"은 단풍 시즌.

#### Sources

- See also: [[months-vocabulary]]

---

business-basics.md.body:
---
title: "business-basics (Korean) expressions"
language: "Korean"
category: "business-basics"
level: "B1-C1"
---

# Expressions: Business Basics (한국어)

> **Theme:** Business & Professional
> **Level:** B1-C1 (formal)
> **Standard:** 표준어 (Pyojuneo, Standard Korean)

Korean business communication — greetings, email/meeting phrases, negotiations, contracts.

---

## 안녕하세요

(See daily-life)

---

## 감사합니다

(See daily-life)

---

## 죄송합니다

(See daily-life)

---

## 잘 부탁드립니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (formal request, greeting)
**Definition:** "Please take care of me" — 가장 격식 있는 인사와 부탁.
**Form:** Jal butak deurimnida.

### Usage

비즈니스 첫 만남, 이메일/문자 시작/끝, 격식 부탁.

### Variations

- **잘 부탁드립니다 (Jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please take care of me" (default 격식)
- **잘 부탁해요 (Jal butakhaeyo)** — "Please take care of me" (정중)
- **잘 부탁해 (Jal butakhae)** — 캐주얼 (친구/동료)
- **부탁드립니다 (Butak deurimnida)** — "Please" (간결)
- **많은 도움 부탁드립니다 (Manyu doum butak deurimnida)** — "Please help me a lot"

### Sample Sentences

- **저희 회사와 잘 부탁드립니다 (Jeohui hoewa jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please take care of our company"
- **앞으로도 잘 부탁드립니다 (Apeurodo jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please continue to take care of me"

### Cultural Notes

- **비즈니스**: 가장 흔한 격식 인사
- **이메일 끝**: "감사합니다, 잘 부탁드립니다" — 두 표현 함께 사용
- **첫 만남**: 명함 교환 시 "잘 부탁드립니다"
- **일본어 "よろしくお願いします (yoroshiku onegaishimasu)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`
- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 수고하셨습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (greeting, workplace)
**Definition:** "Thank you for your hard work" — 직장/동료 표준 인사.
**Form:** Sugo hasyeotseumnida.

### Usage

직장, 회의 종료, 프로젝트 완료.

### Variations

- **수고하셨습니다 (Sugo hasyeotseumnida)** — "Thank you for hard work" (default)
- **수고했어요 (Sugohaesseoyo)** — 캐주얼
- **수고하셨어요 (Sugohasyeosseoyo)** — 캐주얼 변형
- **수고해요 (Sugohaeyo)** — 매우 캐주얼
- **고생하셨습니다 (Gosaeng hasyeotseumnida)** — 격식 (동사)

### Sample Sentences

- **수고하셨습니다, 오늘 회의 마무리 (Sugo hasyeotseumnida, oneul hoeui mamuri)** — "Thank you for your work, ending today's meeting"
- **모두 수고하셨습니다 (Modu sugo hasyeotseumnida)** — "Everyone, thanks for hard work"

### Cultural Notes

- **매일 아침/저녁**: 출근/퇴근 인사
- **상사**: "수고하셨습니다" 정중
- **동료**: "수고했어" / "수고" 캐주얼
- **일본어 "お疲れ様でした"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/cultural-values]]`

---

## 검토하겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (decision)
**Definition:** "I'll review/consider it" — 부드러운 보류.
**Form:** Geomto hagetseumnida.

### Usage

상사/고객의 요청에 즉답 못할 때.

### Variations

- **검토하겠습니다 (Geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll review" (default)
- **검토 후 답변 드리겠습니다 (Geomto hu dapdun deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll answer after review"
- **내일까지 검토해 보겠습니다 (Naeilkkaji geomtohae bogetseumnida)** — "I'll review by tomorrow"
- **신중히 검토하겠습니다 (Sinjunghi geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll carefully review" (강조)

### Sample Sentences

- **요청 사항 검토하겠습니다 (Yocheong saenghwan geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll review your request"
- **내일까지 검토 후 연락 드리겠습니다 (Naeilkkaji geomto hu yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you by tomorrow after review"

### Cultural Notes

- **"검토" = "consider"**: 직접 거절 어려움 (보류 표현)
- **한국 비즈니스**: 정중 거절 = "검토 중"
- **명확한 시간 명시**: 보류 시 응답 시간 명시
- **일본어 "検討します (Kentō shimasu)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 알겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (acknowledgment)
**Definition:** "Understood" — 정중한 동의/수락.
**Form:** Algesseumnida.

### Usage

상사/고객의 지시 수락, 이메일/문자 응답.

### Variations

- **알겠습니다 (Algesseumnida)** — "Understood" (default 격식)
- **알았어요 (Alasseoyo)** — 캐주얼
- **알았어 (Alasseo)** — 매우 캐주얼
- **네, 알겠습니다 (Ne, algesseumnida)** — "Yes, understood"
- **충분히 알겠습니다 (Chungbunhi algesseumnida)** — "Understood thoroughly" (강조)

### Sample Sentences

- **네, 알겠습니다 (Ne, algesseumnida)** — "Yes, understood"
- **말씀하신 내용 잘 알겠습니다 (Malsseum hasin naeyong jal algesseumnida)** — "I understand what you said well"

### Cultural Notes

- **상사**: "알겠습니다" 정중
- **동료**: "알겠어" / "ㅇㅇ (응)" 캐주얼
- **카톡/문자**: "넵 (nep)" = 젊은 세대 "네"
- **일본어 "承知しました"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 죄송하지만

**Part of Speech:** expression (apology, polite transition)
**Definition:** "I'm sorry but..." — 부드러운 거절/중단 표현.
**Form:** Joesonghajiman.

### Usage

요청 거절, 대화 중단, 부정 답변.

### Variations

- **죄송하지만 (Joesonghajiman)** — "I'm sorry but" (default)
- **죄송합니다만 (Joesonghamnidaman)** — 같은 의미 (격식)
- **죄송합니다 (Joesonghamnida)** — 사과만
- **죄송한데요 (Joesonghandeyo)** — 캐주얼
- **미안한데 (Mianhande)** — "Sorry but" (캐주얼)

### Sample Sentences

- **죄송하지만, 참석이 어렵습니다 (Joesonghajiman, chamseogi eoryeopseumnida)** — "Sorry, attendance is difficult"
- **죄송하지만, 그건 어렵습니다 (Joesonghajiman, geugeon eoryeopseumnida)** — "Sorry, that's difficult"

### Cultural Notes

- **정중 거절**: "죄송하지만" = 부드러운 거절
- **실제 거절**: "그건 어렵습니다" / "상황이 어렵습니다" / "검토하겠습니다"
- **한국 문화**: 직접 거절 = 무례, 간접 = 정중
- **일본어 "申し訳ございません"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 확인 부탁드립니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (request, business)
**Definition:** "Please confirm" — 비즈니스 확인 요청.
**Form:** Hwagin butak deurimnida.

### Usage

이메일, 문서 검토, 사실 확인.

### Variations

- **확인 부탁드립니다 (Hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm" (default)
- **확인 부탁해요 (Hwagin butakhaeyo)** — 정중
- **확인 부탁 (Hwagin butak)** — 캐주얼
- **확인 부탁드립니다만 (Hwagin butak deurimnidaman)** — 매우 정중

### Sample Sentences

- **일정 확인 부탁드립니다 (Iljeong hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm the schedule"
- **첨부파일 확인 부탁드립니다 (Cheombupail hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm the attached file"

### Cultural Notes

- **이메일**: "확인 부탁드립니다" + "감사합니다"
- **상사/거래처**: 매우 정중한 표현
- **CC 포함**: 중요 메일은 CC 추가
- **일본어 "ご確認ください (gokakunin kudasai)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`

---

## 연락 드리겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (action)
**Definition:** "I'll contact you" — 후속 연락 약속.
**Form:** Yeollak deurigetseumnida.

### Usage

이메일/문자/전화로 후속 연락 약속.

### Variations

- **연락 드리겠습니다 (Yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you" (default 격식)
- **다시 연락 드리겠습니다 (Dasi yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you again"
- **곧 연락 드리겠습니다 (Got yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you soon"
- **다음 주에 연락 드리겠습니다 (Daeum jue yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you next week"

### Sample Sentences

- **검토 후 연락 드리겠습니다 (Geomto hu yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you after review"
- **확인되는 대로 연락 드리겠습니다 (Hwagindoeneun daero yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you once confirmed"

### Cultural Notes

- **시간 명시**: 명확한 응답 시간 명시
- **약속 후 실행**: 한국 문화는 약속 중요 (실행 필수)
- **지연 시**: 미리 연락 (정중)
- **일본어 "ご連絡いたします (go-renraku itashimasu)"**와 일치

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`

## 업무 단어 & 표현 (Business terms & expressions)

> **Note (2026-07-28)**: 4개 단일 표현 (수고하세요, 열공하세요, 요약, 죄송합니다만) 가 per-word `.md` 스텁에서 본 theme-file 로 통합됨. 이전 per-word 페이지 inbound link 는 모두 `''X''` italic 으로 변환.

### 수고하세요 (sugo-haseyo)

**Part of Speech:** 서술어 (polite acknowledgment of work)

**Definition:** "You've worked hard." — 직장/학교/서비스에서 마주칠 때 정중한 인사/인정 표현.

**Romaja:** sugo-haseyo

**Etymology:** 수고 (辛苦, 한자어 "effort/hardship") + 하 (verb) + 세요 (polite ending).

#### Examples

- 회의 수고하셨습니다. — Thank you for your work in the meeting. (formal closing)
- 오늘 현장 수고하셨어요. — Thank you for your work at the site today. (direct superior → subordinate)

#### Related Terms

- *수고해요* — same, casual/polite mix
- *고생했어요* — same meaning, more colloquial

#### Cultural Notes

- 회의/이메일/SMS 끝에 자주 등장 ("수고하셨습니다" = "thank you for your effort")
- 직장 동료끼리는 일상적, 거래처/상사에게는 격식 더 필요 (수고하셨습니다)
- 학생 → 선생님: "수고하셨습니다" (less common; usually 선생님 → 학생)

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 열공하세요 (yeol-gong-haseyo)

**Part of Speech:** 서술어 (encouragement)

**Definition:** "Study/work hard." — 시험/자격증/작업 마감을 앞둔 사람에게 쓰는 격려 표현.

**Romaja:** yeol-gong-haseyo

**Etymology:** 열공 (熱功, 한자어 약어 "열심히 공부하다") + 하 + 세요. 신조어 (1990년대 이후 학생 문화에서 유래).

#### Examples

- 시험 기간 화이팅, 열공하세요! — Good luck on exams, study hard!
- 프로젝트 마감까지 일주일, 모두 열공합시다. — One week until project deadline, let's all work hard.

#### Related Terms

- *열공합시다* — let's all study/work hard (group exhortation)
- *화이팅* — fighting! (English loanword, similar encouragement)
- *파이팅* — variant pronunciation

#### Cultural Notes

- 학생·수험생 문화에서 광범위 사용
- 직장에서는 "열공하세요" 보다 "열심히 해 주세요" 또는 "마감 잘 부탁드립니다" 가 더 격식적
- 신조어이지만 표준어 등재 (열심히 공부하다의 약자)

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 요약 (yoyak)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (summary) / 동사 (to summarize)

**Definition:** Summary, recapitulation. 회의/보고서/발표 끝에 핵심만 압축한 요점 정리.

**Romaja:** yoyak

**Etymology:** 要約 (한자어, 日語 영향). 동사형: 요약하다 → 요약했어요 / 요약됩니다.

#### Examples

- 오늘 회의 내용을 3가지로 요약하겠습니다. — Let me summarize today's meeting in 3 points.
- 보고서 마지막 장은 결론 및 요약입니다. — The last chapter of the report is conclusion and summary.

#### Related Terms

- *요점* — key point
- *개요* — outline, abstract
- *정리* — 정리하다 (to organize/summarize, more casual)

#### Cultural Notes

비즈니스: 회의록 → 보고서 → 발표 의 흐름에서 "요약" 단계 필수. 5W1H 원칙 적용. 한국 비즈니스 문서는 일반적으로 본문 + 별도 "요약" 섹션 구조.

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 죄송합니다만 (joesong-hamnida-man)

**Part of Speech:** 종속절 (formal apology connector)

**Definition:** "Excuse me / I'm sorry, but..." — 정중한 打斷 (interruption) 또는 요청 도입부.

**Romaja:** joesong-hamnida-man

**Etymology:** 죄송 (罪悚, 한자어 "guilt") + 합니다 (formal polite) + 만 ("but/however" connector).

#### Examples

- 죄송합니다만, 잠깐 시간 있으세요? — Excuse me, do you have a moment?
- 죄송합니다만 다시 한번 말씀해 주시겠어요? — Sorry, could you say that again?

#### Related Terms

- *실례합니다만* — Excuse me (formal, e.g., 회의 중)
- *방해해도 될까요* — May I interrupt?
- *죄송한데* — same, casual/contracted

#### Cultural Notes

- 회의/통화에서 본격적인 요청·打斷 전에 사용 → 한국 비즈니스 매너의 핵심
- "죄송합니다만" 의 함축 의미: "나는 이 요청이 당신에게 부담임을 안다" → 부담 경감 후속 발화 가능
- 너무 자주 사용 시 오히려 진정성 의문 → 정당한 경우에만

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

american-mlk-day.md.title: American Martin Luther King Jr. Day
american-mlk-day.md.body:
# American Martin Luther King Jr. Day

**Overview:** Martin Luther King Jr. Day (third Monday of January) is a federal holiday honoring the birthday of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. (January 15, 1929 — assassinated April 4, 1968). Signed into federal law in 1983 and first observed as a federal holiday in 1986, it is the only U.S. federal holiday commemorating a person who was not a president.

## Key Points

- **1983 Federal Holiday**: President Ronald Reagan signed the King Holiday Bill on November 2, 1983. The first federal observance was January 20, 1986. The holiday is observed on the third Monday of January, near King's January 15 birthday.
- **Civil Rights Legacy**: King led the Montgomery bus boycott (1955-1956), helped found the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC, 1957), led the March on Washington (1963), and won the Nobel Peace Prize (1964). His "I Have a Dream" speech and "Letter from Birmingham Jail" are foundational American texts.
- **"Day of Service, Not a Day Off"**: The King Center and Corporation for National and Community Service promote MLK Day as a day of community service. AmeriCorps holds annual service projects. Many schools and companies organize volunteer activities.
- **Slow State Adoption**: Despite federal recognition, some states resisted. South Carolina was the last state to recognize the holiday (in 2000) as a paid holiday for state employees, following a 1999 NASCAR boycott controversy.
- **Coined with "MLK Day"**: Combines the civil rights leader's initials with the day abbreviation, distinct from generic federal holidays.
- **"I Have a Dream" Speech Anniversary**: The 1963 March on Washington, where King delivered the speech at the Lincoln Memorial, drew 250,000 attendees and helped build momentum for the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
- **Southern States and "King-Lee Day"**: In Arkansas, Alabama, and Mississippi (until 2000), the holiday was combined with Robert E. Lee Day as "King-Lee Day," which civil rights advocates criticized as minimizing King's legacy.

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국은 5월 1일 노동절 (Labor Day) 과 8월 15일 광복절이 가장 가까운 명절. 한국의 현충일 (6월 6일) 이 추모의 역할. 미국 MLK Day 와 같은 시민영웅 추모 명절이 없음. 최근 5·18 민주화 운동 기념일 (5월 18일, 1997년 지정) 이 가장 비슷한 시민의례.
- **Japonés**: 일본 2월 11일 建國記念の日 (건국기념일) 는 신화적 건국일. 미국 MLK Day 처럼 특정 인물 추모는 11월 3일 文化の日 (Bunka no Hi) 가 비슷한 구조. 일본은 개인 인물 추모가 명절이 되는 경우가 거의 없음.
- **Chino**: 중국은 4월 4-5일 청명 (清明) 이 추모 명절이지만 미국 MLK Day 처럼 시민 영웅 추모가 아님. 9월 10일 教师节 (스승의 날) 이 가장 가까운 인물 추모일. 미국식 시민운동 기념일은 없음.

## Examples

«Martin Luther King Jr. Day, observed on the third Monday of January, honors the civil rights leader who advocated for racial equality through nonviolent protest.»

1월 셋째 주 월요일에 기념되는 Martin Luther King Jr. Day 는 비폭력 시위를 통해 인종 평등을 옹호한 민권운동 지도자를 기립니다.

«King's "I Have a Dream" speech, delivered at the March on Washington in 1963, has become one of the most famous speeches in American history.»

1963년 워싱턴 행진에서 행해진 King 의 "I Have a Dream" 연설은 미국 역사에서 가장 유명한 연설 중 하나가 되었습니다.

«Many Americans honor MLK Day by participating in community service projects rather than treating the day as simply a day off work.»

많은 미국인들은 MLK Day 를 단순한 휴무일이 아닌 지역 봉사 활동에 참여함으로써 기념합니다.

american-standup-comedy.md.title: American Stand-Up Comedy
american-standup-comedy.md.body:
# American Stand-Up Comedy

**Overview:** Stand-up comedy is a distinctive American entertainment form in which a single comedian performs live, telling jokes and observational commentary directly to an audience. Originating in vaudeville and Borscht Belt resorts, modern stand-up has evolved through the New York and Los Angeles club scenes into a podcast-dominated era where comedians build global audiences without traditional TV deals.

## Key Points

- **NYC and LA Club Scenes**: New York (Comedy Cellar, Caroline's, Stand Up NY) and Los Angeles (Comedy Store, Laugh Factory, Improv) are the two epicenters. The Comedy Cellar has featured nearly every major comedian of the last 40 years.
- **Open Mic Culture**: Open mics (free or low-cost performances where aspiring comedians try new material) are the entry point. NYC's Comic Strip Live, The Stand, and countless bars host nightly open mics. Comics typically perform 5-10 minutes and refine jokes over dozens of sets.
- **Mitzvah Circuit**: Comics, especially Jewish-American ones, performed at bar mitzvahs and weddings during lean years. The term "working the Borscht Belt" refers to the 1920s-1980s Catskills comedy resorts. Don Rickles, Mel Brooks, Jerry Seinfeld all worked the circuit.
- **Late Night TV as Springboard**: The Tonight Show, Late Show, and SNL have launched countless careers. Jerry Seinfeld's "The Tonight Show" appearances in the 1980s are credited with helping build his material for "Seinfeld."
- **Movers and Shakers**:
  - **Lenny Bruce (1950s-60s)**: Transformed stand-up with social commentary; arrested for obscenity (1961, 1964).
  - **Richard Pryor (1970s-80s)**: Brought raw personal storytelling to mainstream.
  - **George Carlin (1970s-2000s)**: Wordplay and counterculture commentary.
  - **Eddie Murphy (1980s)**: Made comedy concerts into major films (Delirious, 1983; Raw, 1987).
  - **Dave Chappelle (2000s-present)**: His Chappelle's Show (2003-2006) and Netflix specials define modern stand-up.
- **Podcast Era**: Since the 2010s, comedians have built audiences through podcasts (Marc Maron's WTF, Joe Rogan's The Joe Rogan Experience). Rogan signed a $100M Spotify deal in 2020. The 2024 Netflix-curated comedy boom continued the trend.
- **Tight Five / Tight Ten**: A "tight five" is 5 minutes of well-rehearsed, polished material. Most working comedians have multiple tight fives for different sets (clubs, TV, corporate gigs).

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국 개그 문화 — 코미디 프로그램 "개그 콘서트" (1999-2020) + 토크쇼. KBS 개그맨 + "웃찾사" (웃음찾기). 미국 stand-up 보다는 TV 개그 (sitcom) 중심. 한국에는 stand-up 클럽 문화가 약함 (홍대 소수).
- **Japonés**: 일본 お笑い (owarai) — 漫才 (manzai, 둘이서 농담 주고받기), コント (skit), ピン芸 (single comedian). 일본형 stand-up 은 漫才 중심. 미국과 다른 둘이서 호흡 구조. 吉本興業 (Yoshimoto Kogyo) 가 업계 지배.
- **Chino**: 중국 脱口秀 (tuōkǒu xiù, "탈口秀") — 미국식 stand-up 의 중국 수입. 上海, 北京 의 클럽 중심. 杨笠, 何广智, 周奇墨 등이 인기. 2023년 House (喜剧之王) 같은 TV 쇼가 인플루언스. 중국 정치적 한계 (정치 풍자 금지).

## Examples

«Stand-up comedy originated in American vaudeville and Borscht Belt resorts of the early 20th century before evolving into the modern club and podcast format.»

Stand-up comedy 는 20세기 초 미국 vaudeville 과 Borscht Belt 리조트에서 유래한 후, 현대 클럽과 팟캐스트 형식으로 발전했습니다.

«Open mics at clubs like the Comedy Cellar in New York give aspiring comedians the chance to try new material in front of a live audience for free or low cost.»

뉴욕의 Comedy Cellar 같은 클럽의 오픈마이크는 야심 있는 개그맨들에게 무료 또는 저비용으로 라이브 청중 앞에서 새로운 재료를 시도할 기회를 제공합니다.

«Comedians like Dave Chappelle have built global audiences through streaming specials and podcasts, bypassing traditional television networks entirely.»

Dave Chappelle 같은 개그맨들은 스트리밍 스페셜과 팟캐스트를 통해 전통적인 텔레비전 네트워크를 완전히 우회하면서 글로벌 청중을 구축했습니다.

american-food-history.md.title: American Food History
american-food-history.md.body:
# American Food History

**Overview:** American cuisine developed through layers of immigration, regional adaptation, and indigenous influence. European settlers, enslaved Africans, Latin American migrants, and Asian immigrants each contributed dishes and techniques, producing a national food identity that is regional, hybrid, and constantly reinventing itself.

## Key Points

- **Indigenous roots**: Pre-Columbian staples include corn (maize), beans, squash, turkey, and chili peppers. Many "American" foods (cornbread, succotash, pemmican, maple syrup) descend directly from Native American cooking.
- **Thanksgiving origins**: A 1621 harvest meal in Plymouth Colony shared between English Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people. Mythologized as the "first Thanksgiving," though similar harvest feasts had occurred earlier in English and Native traditions.
- **Colonial era (1600s-1700s)**: English, Dutch, German, and Scots-Irish settlers brought stews, puddings, pies, sausages, and bread baking. Regional ingredients (New England cod, Southern pork) shaped local dishes.
- **Enslaved African contributions**: Soul food in the American South — collard greens, black-eyed peas, fried chicken, mac and cheese, cornbread, gumbo — draws directly on West and Central African cooking, adapted to Southern ingredients.
- **Immigration waves (1800s-1900s)**: Italian (pizza, pasta), Jewish (bagels, deli sandwiches), Chinese (chop suey, then Cantonese restaurant food), Irish (corned beef), German (sausage, beer) all became mainstream American food.
- **Regional cuisines**:
  - **Tex-Mex**: Texas-Mexican border cooking. Chili con carne, fajitas, breakfast tacos, queso. Distinct from interior Mexican food.
  - **Cajun / Creole**: Louisiana. French and Spanish influence with African and Caribbean layers. Gumbo, jambalaya, étouffée, beignets.
  - **New England**: Clam chowder (especially Boston's cream-based version), lobster rolls, baked beans, Boston cream pie.
  - **California**: Fusion, fresh produce, farm-to-table movement (1970s+).
- **Fast food as global export**: McDonald's, KFC, and Burger King, all founded in the US (1940s-1950s), reshaped global eating habits and became symbols of American culture worldwide.

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국 음식은 미국보다 강한 국가 정체성 (김치, 된장찌개, 불고기) 을 가지지만, 1980년대 이후 미국식 빵, 피자, 햄버거가 일상화. 한국에는 강한 regional food (전주 한정판, 부산 어묵) 가 있고, 미국 BBQ 와 비슷한 패턴.
- **Japonés**: 일본 洋食 (yōshoku, Western-style food) 는 메이지 시대 이후 미국/유럽 요리를 일본식으로 변형 — 카레라이스, 돈까스, 햄버거. 미국이 세계로 수출한 햄버거는 일본에서 완전히 재창조됨. 일본 ラーメン 도 중국에서 수입 후 일본화.
- **Chino**: 중국 음식은 미국에서 "Chinese food" 라는 범주로 뭉뚱그려지지만, 실제로 사천, 광둥, 상하이는 완전히 다름. 중국 요리사는 19세기 미국에 이민해 철도 노동자 식사를 준비했고, chop suey 가 미국에서 발명된 것으로 알려져 있음.
- **Español**: 스페인 요리 (paella, tapas, jamón) 는 강한 국가 정체성을 유지. 멕시코 요리는 스페인 식민지 영향 + 토착 원주민 영향 (corn, beans, chili), 미국 Tex-Mex 의 원형. 푸에르토리코 요리 (mofongo, arroz con habichuelas) 도 미국 내에서 중요한 지역 음식.

## Examples

«Tex-Mex, like fajitas and chili con carne, started along the Texas-Mexico border and became popular across the US in the twentieth century.» (페히타와 칠리 콘 카르네 같은 Tex-Mex 는 텍사스-�시코 국경을 따라 시작되어 20세기 미국 전역으로 퍼졌다.)

«Soul food in the American South, including collard greens and mac and cheese, has deep roots in West and Central African cooking traditions.» (콜라드 그린과 맥앤치즈를 포함한 미국 남부의 "soul food" 는 서아프리카와 중앙아프리카 요리 전통에 깊은 뿌리를 두고 있다.)

«McDonald's, founded in California in 1940, became one of the biggest symbols of American culture around the world.» (1940년 캘리포니아에서 설립된 맥도날드는 전 세계에서 미국 문화의 가장 큰 상징 중 하나가 되었다.)

english-dating-culture.md.title: English Dating Culture
english-dating-culture.md.body:
# English Dating Culture

**Type:** romance, social-ritual
**Region:** US / UK / Canada / Australia (English-speaking countries)

## Overview

English-speaking countries (especially US) have **explicit, individualist** dating culture. Romantic intent is usually stated clearly, consent is verbal, and personal boundaries are respected. Modern dating emphasizes direct communication, gender equality (in principle), and emotional honesty.

## Setting

A first date in the US/UK: **coffee shop, restaurant, bar, or walk in a park**. Evening (7-9pm typical). Casual to smart-casual dress. Two people meeting with romantic intent, getting to know each other.

## Roles

- **Person who invites (inviter)** — takes initiative, suggests time/place
- **Invitee** — can accept, suggest alternatives, or decline politely
- Both pay attention to comfort, consent, and clear communication

## Scenario: A Typical First Date

1. **Planning** — Inviter suggests a specific time/place ("Want to grab coffee Saturday at 3?")
2. **Acceptance** — Invitee confirms or reschedules
3. **Arrival** — Both arrive on time (5 min early is normal); greet with smile + light hug or wave
4. **Conversation** — Mix of light (hobbies, work) and deeper (values, life goals) topics
5. **Physical contact** — Wait for clear signals; ask before initiating hand-holding or kissing
6. **Bill** — Often offered by inviter, but splitting is normal; "Let's split?" is OK
7. **End** — Confirm interest: "I had a great time, want to do this again?"
8. **Follow-up text** — Within 24 hours: "Thanks for tonight, I really enjoyed it."

## Cultural Insight

### "Hanging Out" vs "Dating"

In US English, "date" implies **explicit romantic intent**. "Hang out" is ambiguous — could be friends or romantic. Modern dating advice encourages **clarifying intent early** to avoid misunderstandings.

**"Are we hanging out or dating?"** is a real conversation that happens. Best to be clear from the start.

### Splitting the Bill

**Generation gap**:
- Older generations: man traditionally pays
- Younger (Z, Millennials): 50/50 split is normal
- Most common: person who invited pays, but offering to split is polite

**Tactful**: Don't insist either way. "Let's split it?" or "I've got this one" are both fine.

### Consent Culture

Modern English-speaking countries (especially US/Canada/UK) have embraced **explicit verbal consent**:
- "Can I hold your hand?"
- "Can I kiss you?"
- "Is this okay?"

Not asking is now considered a **red flag**. Asking is **mature**, not awkward.

### "I Love You" Timing

- **US**: typically 2-3 months into a relationship
- **UK**: often later (3-6 months)
- **Australia**: relatively early (1-2 months)

Earlier expression: "I really like you" (more universally safe).

### Personal Space

- **Friends/acquaintances**: ~45cm (18in)
- **Romantic partners**: closer, touching common
- **Strangers**: arm's length+

**Eye contact**: 60-70% during conversation = interested.

### Online / Text Dating

- **Apps**: Tinder, Bumble, Hinge dominant in US/UK
- **First contact**: text/messaging common
- **Phone call**: more sincere, less common
- **Asking out**: text is fine; in-person or call for serious intent

## Useful Phrases

- i-like-you — early affection
- i-love-you — deep feeling
- beautiful — appearance compliment
- handsome — male appearance compliment
- kind — personality compliment
- can-i-kiss-you — consent request
- would-you-like-to — invitation
- i-had-a-great-time — end-of-date
- see-you-again — follow-up

## What NOT to Do

- ❌ **"Wanna date?"** in first message — too direct
- ❌ **Bombarding texts** — turn-off
- ❌ **"You up?"** late-night texts — usually means casual sex
- ❌ **Love bombing** — excessive flattery early
- ❌ **Ghosting** — disappearing without explanation (avoidable but common)
- ❌ **"You're so beautiful"** to a stranger on the street — catcalling, harassment
- ❌ **Asking weight, age, salary** on first date — too personal
- ❌ **Talking only about yourself** — reciprocal conversation expected

## Body Language

| Gesture | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Eye contact 60-70% | Interested, engaged |
| Mirroring (leaning in, gestures) | Comfortable, in sync |
| Looking at phone during date | Disinterested, rude |
| Fidgeting, looking around | Nervous or bored |
| Touching face/hair (other person) | Often flirting, but not always |
| Hand on table palm up | Inviting touch |
| Turning body toward you | Engaged |

## Cross-Reference

- Compare with: [[japanese-dating-culture]], [[spanish-dating-culture]], [[korean-dating-culture]]
- See also: i-love-you, beautiful, handsome

## Holiday / Special Days

- **Valentine's Day** (Feb 14) — big romantic holiday
- **Anniversaries** — celebrate relationship start
- **No formal "100 days" celebration** (unlike Korean culture)

## Examples

"Coffee date" — first-date archetype in US urban culture, neutral public setting.
"Hinge" (launched 2012) — dating app designed for "designed to be deleted" with relationship focus.
"Ghosting" — abruptly cutting off all communication without explanation, common post-2010s dating culture phenomenon.

---

## Sources

- [[dating-romance]] — main source
- BBC Learning English — Relationships
- The Atlantic — Modern dating essays
- OKCupid / Hinge dating blog posts
- Consent culture resources (Planned Parenthood, etc.)

american-civil-rights-movement.md.body:
# American Civil Rights Movement

**Overview:** The American Civil Rights Movement (roughly 1954-1968) was a mass mobilization of Black Americans and allies challenging racial segregation, disenfranchisement, and violence in the Jim Crow South. The movement produced landmark legislation (Civil Rights Act of 1964, Voting Rights Act of 1965) and reshaped American law, politics, and culture.

## Key Points

- **Background: Jim Crow South**: From the 1870s through the 1960s, Southern states enforced racial segregation in schools, public facilities, transportation, and voting (poll taxes, literacy tests). Black Americans faced systemic violence (lynching) and economic exclusion.
- **Brown v. Board of Education (1954)**: Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional. The case, argued by Thurgood Marshall, overturned the "separate but equal" doctrine from Plessy v. Ferguson (1896).
- **Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-1956)**: Rosa Parks's arrest (December 1, 1955) for refusing to give up her bus seat sparked a 381-day boycott. Martin Luther King Jr. emerged as a national leader. The Supreme Court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional.
- **Greensboro Sit-Ins (1960)**: Four Black college students sat at a segregated Woolworth's lunch counter in North Carolina, sparking a wave of nonviolent sit-ins. The Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) formed from these efforts.
- **March on Washington (August 28, 1963)**: 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial. King's "I Have a Dream" speech defined the movement. The march helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
- **Civil Rights Act of 1964**: Banned segregation in public accommodations and employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. Endorsed by President Lyndon B. Johnson.
- **Voting Rights Act of 1965**: Outlawed discriminatory voting practices. Within five years, Black voter registration in the Deep South rose from 23% to 61%. Later weakened by Shelby County v. Holder (2013).
- **Assassinations**: Martin Luther King Jr. (April 4, 1968) and Robert F. Kennedy (June 5, 1968) were assassinated. Riots erupted in over 100 U.S. cities after King's death.

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국 5·18 민주화 운동 (1980, 광주) — 군부 독재에 대한 시민 저항. 미국 시민권운동과 같은 비폭력 시민 저항이지만 미국은 "인종 평등", 한국은 "민주주의" 가 핵심. 한국 진보운동의 중요한 레퍼런스.
- **Japonés**: 일본에는 미국식 시민권운동 없음. 部落問題 (Buraku mondai) — 차별받는 소수민족 문제는 비슷하지만 광범위한 시민 운동으로는 전개되지 않음. 미국 시민권운동은 1960년대 일본 지식인에게 큰 영향.
- **Chino**: 중국에는 미국식 시민권운동 없음. 중화민국 (대만) 시절 228 사건 (1947) 이 비슷하지만 국제적 주목을 받지 못함. 중국 본토의 反右 (1957) 운동은 비판 박살.

## Examples

«Rosa Parks's arrest in Montgomery, Alabama in 1955 sparked a 381-day bus boycott that brought Martin Luther King Jr. to national prominence.»

1955년 앨라배마 몽고메리에서 Rosa Parks 의 체포는 381일 동안 계속된 버스 보이콧을 촉발시켰고, 이는 Martin Luther King Jr. 를 전국적 저명 인물로 이끌었습니다.

«The Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed discriminatory voting practices such as literacy tests, dramatically increasing Black voter registration in the Southern United States.»

1965년의 Voting Rights Act 는 문해력 시험과 같은 차별적 투표 관행을 금지하여, 미국 남부에서 흑인 유권자 등록률을 크게 증가시켰습니다.

«The March on Washington in August 1963 drew 250,000 people to the Lincoln Memorial, where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his "I Have a Dream" speech.»

1963년 8월 워싱턴 행진은 25만명을 링컨 기념관으로 끌어모았고, Martin Luther King Jr. 는 그곳에서 "I Have a Dream" 연설을 했습니다.

# Movie Quotes (English)

**Source:** [[movie-quotes]]
**Theme:** Movies / Entertainment
**Level:** B1-C1 (Intermediate-Advanced)

Iconic lines from famous movies. Useful for cultural understanding, conversation practice, and learning natural English expressions through film dialogue.

## Famous Iconic Quotes

### "May the Force be with you."

**Source:** Star Wars (1977)

**Meaning:** 은하 제국의 팰퍼시트 (= 별의 전쟁) 시리즈

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- Force — 힘, 힘 (초자연적 힘)
- be with you — 너와 함께하다

#### Cultural Impact

- 영화 역사상 가장 유명한 대사 중 하나
- AFI (American Film Institute) 100대 명대사 중 8위
- "Star Wars" 시리즈 전편에 등장

### "I'll be back."

**Source:** The Terminator (1984)

**Meaning:** 다시 돌아오겠다

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- I'll — I will (축약형)
- be back — 돌아오다

#### Cultural Impact

- 아놀드 슈워제네거의 시그니처 대사
- AFI 100대 명대사 중 37위
- 속기 쉬운 짧고 임팩트 있는 대사

### "Here's looking at you, kid."

**Source:** Casablanca (1942)

**Meaning:** 너를 바라보고 있단다

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- Here's — Here is (축약형)
- looking at — 바라보다
- kid — 아이, 젊은이

#### Cultural Impact

- 험프리 보가트의 대표 대사
- AFI 100대 명대사 1위
- "Casablanca" 의 상징적 장면

### "You can't handle the truth!"

**Source:** A Few Good Men (1992)

**Meaning:** 너는 진실을 감당할 수 없어!

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- can't — cannot (축약형)
- handle — 다루다, 감당하다
- truth — 진실

### "Houston, we have a problem."

**Source:** Apollo 13 (1995)

**Meaning:** 휴스턴, 문제가 생겼습니다

#### Cultural Impact

- NASA 실제 사고에서 영감
- 영화 역사상 유명한 대사

# English-Speaking School Culture

**Type:** culture, education, social-norms
**Region:** US / UK / Canada / Australia / NZ

## Overview

English-speaking school culture emphasizes individualism, Socratic discussion, extracurricular activities, and preparing for college admission. The US system differs significantly from UK (more formal), Canadian (similar to US), and Australian/NZ (more casual, less competitive). This page complements `[[english-dating-culture]]`, `[[english-workplace-culture]]`, and `[[american-cultural-values]]`.

## School System Comparison

### Educational Stages

| Stage | Age (approx) | US | UK | Canada | AU |
|-------|-------------|----|----|----|----|
| Pre-K / Reception | 3-5 | Pre-K / Kindergarten | Reception | Junior Kindergarten | Pre-School |
| Elementary / Primary | 5-11 | Elementary (K-5) | Primary (Y1-Y6) | Elementary (K-6) | Primary (K-6) |
| Middle | 11-14 | Middle School (6-8) | — | Middle School (7-9) | — |
| High / Secondary | 14-18 | High School (9-12) | Secondary (Y7-Y13) | Secondary (9-12) | Secondary (7-12) |
| Sixth Form | 16-18 | — | Sixth Form College | — | Year 11-12 |
| University | 18-22 | College / University | University | University | University |

### School Year

| Country | Year Start | Year End |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| **US** | Late August / September | Late May / June |
| **UK** | September | July |
| **Canada** | September | June |
| **AU/NZ** | January / February | November / December |

### School Day Times

| Country | Start | End | Total |
|---------|-------|-----|-------|
| **US (HS)** | 7:30-8:30 AM | 2:30-3:30 PM | 6.5-7 hrs |
| **UK (Sec)** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6.5 hrs |
| **Canada** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6 hrs |
| **AU (Sec)** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6.5 hrs |

---

## Academic Culture

### Class Discussion

| Behavior | US | UK | Canada | AU |
|---------|----|----|----|----|
| Speak up in class | Expected | Encouraged | Expected | Expected |
| Question the teacher | Common | Acceptable | Common | Common |
| Group projects | Standard | Standard | Standard | Standard |
| Socratic method | Common | Common | Common | Less common |
| Call teacher by first name | Common | Rare | Common | Common |

### Grading System

| Country | Scale | "A" Equivalent |
|---------|-------|---------------|
| **US (GPA)** | 0.0-4.0 | 4.0 = A (90-100%) |
| **US (Letter)** | A-F | A+ (97-100) |
| **UK (A-Levels)** | A*-U | A* (90-100%) |
| **UK (GCSE)** | 9-1 | 9 (90-100%) |
| **Canada** | 0-100 | 80+ = A |
| **AU (ATAR)** | 0-99.95 | 99+ (top) |

### College Entrance Exams

| Country | Test | Format | Frequency |
|---------|-------|--------|-----------|
| **US** | SAT / ACT | Multiple choice | Multiple times/year |
| **UK** | A-Levels | Subject-specific | Once (Y13) |
| **Canada** | SAT (similar to US) | Multiple choice | Multiple |
| **AU** | ATAR / HSC / VCE | Subject-specific | Once (Y12) |

---

## School Vocabulary

### People

| EN | Age Range | Notes |
|----|-----------|-------|
| Preschooler | 3-5 | Pre-K |
| Kindergartener | 5-6 | First year of school |
| Elementary schooler | 6-11 | Grades K-5 |
| Middle schooler | 11-14 | Grades 6-8 |
| High schooler | 14-18 | Grades 9-12 |
| Freshman | 14-15 | First year HS |
| Sophomore | 15-16 | Second year HS |
| Junior | 16-17 | Third year HS |
| Senior | 17-18 | Fourth year HS |
| Freshman (college) | 18-19 | First year uni |
| Sophomore | 19-20 | Second year uni |
| Junior | 20-21 | Third year uni |
| Senior | 21-22 | Fourth year uni |

### Places

| EN | Context |
|----|---------|
| Classroom | Standard learning space |
| Lecture hall | College (US) / Uni (UK) |
| Auditorium | All-school assembly space |
| Cafeteria | Where students eat |
| Library | Study / research space |
| Gymnasium | Sports / PE class |
| Hallway | Common transit area |
| Faculty | Teachers' lounge (US) |
| Staff room | Teachers' lounge (UK) |
| Quidditch pitch | Harry Potter only 😉 |

### Supplies

|----|-------------|
| Backpack | Standard carry-all |
| Lunch box / Lunch pail | Carries meal |

| Eraser | Mistakes happen |

| Laptop | Modern standard |

| Thumb drive | Same |

---

## School Subjects

| EN | US | UK | Australia |
|----|----|----|-----------|
| **Math** | Math / Algebra / Geometry / Calculus | Mathematics | Mathematics |
| **Science** | Biology, Chemistry, Physics | Combined Science / Separate Sciences | Science |
| **English** | English / Literature | English Literature | English |
| **History** | US History / World History | History | History |
| **Geography** | Geography | Geography | Geography |
| **PE** | Physical Education (PE) | PE / Games | Health & PE |
| **Music** | Band / Choir / Orchestra | Music | Music |
| **Art** | Art | Art | Visual Arts |
| **Drama** | Drama / Theater | Drama | Drama |
| **Computer** | Computer Science / Technology | ICT (Information & Communication Technology) | Digital Technologies |

---

## High School Experience

### American High School

- **Sports culture**: Football (fall), basketball (winter), baseball/track (spring)
- **Prom** (Junior + Senior)
- **Homecoming** (fall)
- **Graduation** (ceremony + parties)
- **Yearbook**
- **Clubs**: 50+ typical (chess club, robotics, drama, etc.)
- **Lunch**: 30 min, cafeteria or off-campus
- **AP (Advanced Placement) courses**: College credit possible
- **SAT/ACT**: Junior year (optional but important)
- **Extracurriculars**: Critical for college applications
- **Spirit week, homecoming, prom**: Major events

### British High School

- **Sixth Form College** (Y12-Y13): Specialized A-Levels
- **A-Levels**: Subject-specific exams (3-4 subjects)
- **UCAS application**: For university admission
- **House system**: Common (Harry Potter-esque)
- **School uniform**: Standard (formal)
- **Sports**: Rugby, cricket, football (soccer)
- **Formal dinners, speech days**: Major events

### Canadian High School

- Similar to US system
- **Provincial variations** (Ontario, Quebec, BC, Alberta differ)
- **Quebec**: French-language schools (CÉGEP)
- **Sports**: Hockey (Canada's national sport!)
- **Co-op programs**: Work-integrated learning
- **Provincial exams** (varies)

### Australian High School

- **Less competitive** than US/Asia
- **ATAR**: University admission (state-specific)
- **Year 12 final exams**: Major event
- **Schoolies week**: Post-grad celebration
- **Sports**: AFL, cricket, rugby, NRL
- **Uniforms**: Standard (often distinctive colors)
- **Casual, friendly culture**: Less hierarchical than UK

---

## College/University Culture

### American College

- **Dorm life**: Freshman dorms, Greek life
- **Majors**: Declared sophomore year
- **Gen-Ed requirements**: First 2 years
- **Semester system**: Fall/Spring (+ optional Summer)
- **Tuition**: Very high ($30-70K/year private)
- **Sports culture**: NCAA, football Saturdays
- **Greek life (fraternities/sororities)**: Common but controversial

### British University

- **Halls of residence**: First year accommodation
- **Subject-focused**: Apply directly to course
- **3-year undergraduate** (typical, vs. US 4-year)
- **Tutorial system**: Oxford/Cambridge famous
- **Term system**: Michaelmas, Hilary, Trinity (Oxford)
- **Pub culture**: Central to social life
- **Tuition**: £9,250/year (capped for UK students)

### Canadian University

- Similar to US system but cheaper
- **Co-op programs**: Common (work + study)
- **U15 (top universities)**: Toronto, UBC, McGill, etc.
- **French immersion** (Quebec)
- **Undergraduate 4 years** (most programs)

### Australian University

- **3-year undergraduate** (typical)
- **Sandstone universities**: Oldest, prestigious (Melbourne, Sydney)
- **Group of Eight**: Top research universities
- **ATAR-based admission**: Similar to UK
- **Residential colleges**: On-campus accommodation
- **Pub culture**: Very strong (uni bars)
- **Casual, outdoorsy culture**: Less formal than UK

---

## Vocabulary by Activity

### Studying

| "Study for an exam" | Prepare for test |
| "Cram" | Last-minute study |
| "Pull an all-nighter" | Study through the night |
| "Cheat sheet / crib sheet" | Illegal notes used in exam |
| "Cheat" | Use unauthorized help in exam |
| "Office hours" | Professor availability time |
| "TA (Teaching Assistant)" | Graduate student instructor |

### School Events

| **Chancellor** | Head of university system |
| **Tenure** | Permanent faculty position |
| **Sabbatical** | Paid research leave |
| **Dissertation** | Doctoral research paper |
| **Thesis** | Master's research paper |

### "Cram" Culture

| EN | Meaning |
|----|---------|
| "Pull an all-nighter" | Study through the night |
| "Cram session" | Intense study session |
| "Memorize" | Rote learning |
| "Flash cards" | Quick study cards |
| "Cheat sheet" | (Illegal) hidden notes |
| "Senioritis" | Senior year laziness |
| "Brain freeze" | Mental block during test |
| "Go blank" | Mind goes empty |
| "Test anxiety" | Stress before/during exam |

---

## Cultural Tips for Visitors

✅ **Ask about school culture** — Will engage in conversation
✅ **Participate in student activities** — Sports, clubs
✅ **Use "How was school?"** as small talk
✅ **Respect homework culture** — Children are busy
✅ **Try cafeteria food** — Cultural experience
✅ **Attend sports events** — Social bonding

❌ **Don't criticize US testing culture** — Sensitive topic
❌ **Don't ask about college debt** — Common pain point
❌ **Don't assume all schools are same** — US vs UK very different
❌ **Don't ignore dress codes** — Some schools strict
❌ **Don't skip graduation ceremonies** — Important family event

jp-daily-life-vocabulary.md.body:
---
category: "jp-daily-life-vocabulary"
level: "JLPT N5-N4"
---

# 日本語 日常生活動詞 (Daily Life Verbs)

**Language:** Japanese
**Theme:** Daily Activities (日常生活)
**Level:** JLPT N5-N4

毎日に必要な基本動詞を集めた。起きる、寝る、食べる、飲む、行く、来る、働く — すべて日本語教育の初期段階で学習する Group 1 (五段) / Group 2 (一段) の代表動詞。敬語 (尊敬語/謙譲語) の対応形も併せて確認できる。

---

## 起床・就寝 (Waking & Sleeping)

### 起きる

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 2, 一段)

**Definition:** to wake up, to get up

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** おきる (okiru)

**Etymology:** 和語: 起きる (起きる) 自立動詞

#### Examples

- 毎朝 7 時に起きます。 — 習慣
- 早く起きて勉強しました。 — 動作
- 先生はお早くお起きになりました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 起きる — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞
- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]] — 日常生活動詞

#### Cultural Notes

「起きる」と「目覚める」(mezameru) は類義だが、目覚めるはやや文語的・文学的。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 寝る

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 2, 一段)

**Definition:** to sleep, to go to bed

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** ねる (neru)

**Etymology:** 和語: 寝る (寝る) 自立動詞

#### Examples

- 11 時に寝ます。 — 習慣
- 早く寝なければなりません。 — 必要
- 早くお休みください。 — 謙譲語依頼 (就寝)

#### Related Terms

- 寝る — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞

#### Cultural Notes

就寝時に「お休み」(oyasumi) が定型の別れ挨拶。尊敬語では「お休みになる」。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

## 食事 (Eating & Drinking)

### 食べる

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 2, 一段)

**Definition:** to eat

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** たべる (taberu)

**Etymology:** 和語: 食べる (食べる) 他動詞

#### Examples

- 朝ごはんを食べます。 — 動作
- 何を食べたいですか。 — 願望
- 先生がたをお食べになりました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 食べる — 自動参照
- [[jp-restaurant-vocabulary]] — レストラン語彙

#### Cultural Notes

食事前に「いただきます」、食後に「ごちそうさま」(gochisousama) が文化的に必須のマナー。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 飲む

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段)

**Definition:** to drink, to take (medicine)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** のむ (nomu)

**Etymology:** 和語: 飲む (飲む) 他動詞

#### Examples

- 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。 — 習慣
- お薬を飲んでください。 — 依頼
- お酒をお飲みになりますか。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 飲む — 自動参照
- [[jp-restaurant-vocabulary]] — レストラン語彙

#### Cultural Notes

薬を飲む際も「飲む」が使われる (西洋の take medicine と同じ)。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

## 移動 (Movement)

### 行く

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段)

**Definition:** to go

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** いく (iku)

**Etymology:** 和語: 行く (行く) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 学校に行きます。 — 方向
- 明日どこへ行きますか。 — 疑問
- 先生がお行きになりました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 行く — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (へ/に/から)

#### Cultural Notes

「行く」「来る」(kuru) は話者の位置を基準に使い分ける。話し手から離れる方向 = 行く、話し手に向かう方向 = 来る。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 来る

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 3, 不規則)

**Definition:** to come

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** くる (kuru)

**Etymology:** 和語: 来る (来る) 不規則動詞

#### Examples

- 友達が来ました。 — 到着
- いつ来ますか。 — 疑問
- 先生がお越しくださいました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 来る — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞

#### Cultural Notes

不規則動詞で、ます形は「来ます」(kimasu)、て形は「来て」(kite)。JLPT の最重要動詞の一つ。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 帰る

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段)

**Definition:** to return (home), to go back

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** かえる (kaeru)

**Etymology:** 和語: 帰る (帰る) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 6 時に家に帰ります。 — 帰宅
- 早く帰りましょう。 — 提案
- もうお帰りですか。 — 敬語

#### Related Terms

- 帰る — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (に)

#### Cultural Notes

「帰る」は主に「帰宅」、より一般的な「戻る」(modoru) は任意の地点に戻る意味。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

## 労働・活動 (Work & Activities)

### 働く

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段)

**Definition:** to work

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** はたらく (hataraku)

**Etymology:** 和語: 働く (働く) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 東京で働いています。 — 現在
- 一生懸命働いてください。 — 依頼
- 先生はお働きになりました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- 働く — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (で)

#### Cultural Notes

「はたらく」は肉体労働・頭脳労働の両方に使える。日本語の「労働」(roudou) と「仕事」(shigoto) はニュアンスが異なる。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 勉強する

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 3, 不規則 + する)

**Definition:** to study

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** べんきょうする (benkyou suru)

**Etymology:** 漢語: 勉強 (benkyou) + する (suru) = 無理して努力する

#### Examples

- 毎日日本語を勉強します。 — 動作
- 大学で経済学を勉強しました。 — 過去
- お勉強になりますね。 — 謙譲語的

#### Related Terms

- 勉強する — 自動参照
- [[jp-adjectives-vocabulary]] — 形容詞

#### Cultural Notes

「勉強」は元々「無理して努力する」の意。現代では「study」の意味が完全に定着。JLPT N5。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### 遊ぶ

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段)

**Definition:** to play, to hang out

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** あそぶ (asobu)

**Etymology:** 和語: 遊ぶ (遊ぶ) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 子供たちが公園で遊びます。 — 動作
- 昨日友達と遊びました。 — 過去
- お遊びになりますか。 — 尊敬語 (rare)

#### Related Terms

- 遊ぶ — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (で/と)

#### Cultural Notes

「遊ぶ」は子供の遊ぶだけでなく、大人のレジャーや社交にも使われる。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

## 状態・存在 (Existence & States)

### ある

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 1, 五段, 非対格)

**Definition:** to exist (inanimate), to have

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** ある (aru)

**Etymology:** 和語: ある (有る) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 机の上に本があります。 — 存在 (in 場所/に)
- 私はお金があります。 — 所有
- 先生はお車がございますか。 — 謙譲語

#### Related Terms

- ある — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (に/で)

#### Cultural Notes

「ある」(inanimates) と「いる」(animates) の使い分けが必須。所有の「ある」は「が」主語。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### いる

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 2, 一段)

**Definition:** to exist (animate), to be (somewhere), to need (〜がいる)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** いる (iru)

**Etymology:** 和語: いる (居る) 自動詞

#### Examples

- 家に猫がいます。 — 存在
- 東京にいます。 — 位置
- 先生がおいでになります。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- いる — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (に)

#### Cultural Notes

「いる」(animates) vs 「ある」(inanimates) の使い分けは JLPT N5 の最重要文法項目。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

### する

**Part of Speech:** 動詞 (Group 3, 不規則)

**Definition:** to do, to make, to try on

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** する (suru)

**Etymology:** 和語: する (する) 自動詞/他動詞

#### Examples

- 毎日運動をします。 — 動作
- 日本語を勉強します。 — 動作
- 先生がお決めになりました。 — 尊敬語

#### Related Terms

- する — 自動参照
- [[jp-time-prepositions-vocabulary]] — 時間前置詞 (を)

#### Cultural Notes

サ変動詞の代表格で、名詞 + する の形で無数の動詞を派生できる (勉強する, 運動する, 食事する)。

#### Sources

- [[jp-daily-life-vocabulary]]

---

jp-quotes-vocabulary.md.title: 日本語 ことわざ・四字熟語 (Japanese Quotes & Idioms)
jp-quotes-vocabulary.md.body:
---
category: "jp-quotes-vocabulary"
level: "JLPT N3-N1"
---

# 日本語 ことわざ・四字熟語 (Japanese Quotes & Idioms)

**Language:** Japanese
**Theme:** Quotes & Idioms (ことわざ・四字熟語)
**Level:** JLPT N3-N1

日本語の **慣用句 (kan'yoku)** には古来より伝わる **ことわざ (proverb)**、漢語由来の **四字熟語 (yojijukugo)**、現代日本文化に根ざす **名言 (meigen)** がある。日常会話・文章・SNS で幅広く使われ、文化的素養の指標ともなる。

---

## 古典ことわざ (Classical Proverbs)

### 一期一会

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo)

**Definition:** one encounter, one chance (treasure every meeting as once-in-a-lifetime)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** いちごいちえ (ichigo ichie)

**Etymology:** 茶人・千利休の茶道理念に由来。一回きりの出会いを大切にする意

#### Examples

- 一期一会の精神で接客します。 — 商売
- 茶道は一期一会です。 — 茶道
- 今日の出会いを一期一会と思って大切にしよう。 — 人生訓

#### Related Terms

- 一期一会 — 自動参照
- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

茶道 (sadō) の根本理念。日本人の「瞬間」を大切にする精神性を代表する四字熟語。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 七転び八起き

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** fall seven times, stand up eight (perseverance)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** ななころびやおき (nanakorobi yaoki)

**Etymology:** 仏教説話「七番煎じまで薬になる」などに通じる、何度も失敗から立ち直る意

#### Examples

- 七転び八起きの精神で挑戦します。 — 励志
- 人生は七転び八起きだ。 — 一般論
- 彼女は七転び八起きで成功した。 — 人物描写

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

「転ぶ」(korobu) は「倒れる」、八の字は末広がりで縁起が良い。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 花鳥風月

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo)

**Definition:** the beauties of nature (flowers, birds, wind, moon)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** かちょうふうげつ (kachou fuugetsu)

**Etymology:** 中国・白居易の詩に由来。自然の風物を愛でる文化的志向

#### Examples

- 花鳥風月を愛でる。 — 自然観照
- 花鳥風月をテーマにした俳句。 — 文学
- 花鳥風月の暮らし。 — 余暇文化

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

日本の自然観・美意識の根幹を成す概念。俳句・和歌・水墨画など日本芸術の主要テーマ。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 三十六計

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo)

**Definition:** the 36 stratagems (military cunning)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** さんじゅうろっけい (sanjuu rokkei)

**Etymology:** 中国・南北朝時代の兵書『三十六計』より。戦略・駆け引きの代名詞

#### Examples

- 三十六計逃げるにしかず。 — ことわざ完成形
- 三十六計を繰り出す。 — 駆け引き
- 経営戦略に三十六計を生かす。 — 比�

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

「逃げるにしかず」(escape is the best of the 36 stratagems) が定型句で、自己保身を肯定的に表現。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

## 人生・仕事 (Life & Work)

### 失敗は成功のもと

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** failure is the foundation of success

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** しっぱいはせいこうのもと (shippai wa seikou no moto)

**Etymology:** 「失敗」(shippai) + 「成功」(seikou) + 「もと」(moto = foundation)

#### Examples

- 失敗は成功のもとだと思って頑張ります。 — 励志
- 失敗は成功のもとと信じています。 — 信念
- 失敗は成功のもとだから大丈夫です。 — 励まし

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

「失敗を恐れず挑戦しよう」というポジティブシンキングの代名詞。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 猿も木から落ちる

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** even monkeys fall from trees (experts make mistakes too)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** さるもきからおちる (saru mo ki kara ochiru)

**Etymology:** 「猿」(saru = monkey) + 「木」(ki = tree) + 「落ちる」(ochiru = fall)

#### Examples

- 猿も木から落ちる、だから慎重に。 — 警告
- 猿も木から落ちる、失敗もあるさ。 — 慰め
- プロの彼女も猿も木から落ちる。 — 教訓

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

英語 "even Homer sometimes nods" に対応する表現。ベテランの失敗を許容する寛容の精神。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 石の上にも三年

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** three years on a stone (perseverance warms even cold stone)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** いしのうえにもさんねん (ishi no ue ni mo san nen)

**Etymology:** 冷たい石でも 3 年座れば温まる意から。継続の大切さ

#### Examples

- 石の上にも三年、続けます。 — 励志
- 石の上にも三年の精神で。 — 仕事
- 忍耐、石の上にも三年です。 — 教訓

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

辛抱・継続を肯定する日本文化の代表的ことわざ。新人教育でも頻出。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 二度あることは三度ある

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** what happens twice will happen thrice (be careful of repeated patterns)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** にどあることはさんどある (nido aru koto wa sando aru)

**Etymology:** 二度起こったことは三度起こる、という経験則

#### Examples

- 二度あることは三度ある、用心しよう。 — 警告
- 二度あることは三度ある、また失敗した。 — 経験談
- 二度あることは三度あるというから。 — 一般論

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

英語 "third time's the charm" とは逆の教訓。注意喚起に使われる。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

## 人間・社会 (Human Relations & Society)

### 一石二鳥

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo)

**Definition:** killing two birds with one stone

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** いっせきにちょう (isseki nichou)

**Etymology:** 一つの石 (isseki) で二羽の鳥 (nichou) を落とす意

#### Examples

- 一石二鳥の計画です。 — 効率
- 運動と勉強、一石二鳥ですね。 — 複数目的
- 一石二鳥の効果が期待できる。 — 利益

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

英語とほぼ同じ意味・用法。ビジネス・日常会話で頻出。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 魚と熊掌

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo, 中国語由来の故事成語)

**Definition:** fish and bear's paw (can't have both)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** ぎょとゆうしょう (gyo to yuushou)

**Etymology:** 中国『孟子』「魚我所欲也、熊掌亦我所欲也...」(魚は私の欲する所、熊掌もまた...) より。両方取れない二者択一の喩え

#### Examples

- 魚と熊掌は取れない。 — 選択
- 魚と熊掌、どちらか選ばねば。 — ジレンマ
- 魚と熊掌の選択に迫られた。 — 困難

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

日本語では「二者択一」「トレードオフ」とほぼ同義。故事成語として古典素養の指標。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 雨降って地固まる

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** rain falls and the ground hardens (discord leads to stronger bonds)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** あめふってじかたまる (ame futte ji katamaru)

**Etymology:** 雨で地面が固まる意から、争い・試練の後の結束を表す

#### Examples

- 雨降って地固まる、仲直りしました。 — 関係修復
- 雨降って地固まるの言葉どおり。 — 結果
- あの喧嘩も雨降って地固まるでしたね。 — 回顧

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

夫婦・同僚・チームの修復を表すポジティブな表現。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 十人十色

**Part of Speech:** 四字熟語 (yojijukugo)

**Definition:** ten people, ten colors (everyone is different)

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** じゅうにんといろ (juunin toiro)

**Etymology:** 十人 (10 people) + 十色 (10 colors) = 人はそれぞれ異なる

#### Examples

- 十人十色ですから。 — 多様性
- 好みは十人十色です。 — 個人差
- 十人十色の意見を尊重する。 — 価値観

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

多様性 (diversity) を肯定的に表現する現代日本的価値観。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

## 学習・努力 (Learning & Effort)

### 塵も積もれば山となる

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** even dust, when piled up, becomes a mountain

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** ちりもつもればやまとなる (chiri mo tsumoreba yama to naru)

**Etymology:** 小さな努力の蓄積が大きな成果を生む意

#### Examples

- 塵も積もれば山となる、毎日少しずつ。 — 励志
- 塵も積もれば山となる、貯金の力。 — 比喩
- 塵も積もれば山となる、続けた結果は大きい。 — 教訓

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

英語 "many a mickle makes a muckle" に対応する表現。継続を重んじる日本文化。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

---

### 備えあれば憂いなし

**Part of Speech:** ことわざ (proverb)

**Definition:** with preparation, there is no worry

**Reading / Hiragana / Romaji:** そなえあればうれいなし (sonae areba urei nashi)

**Etymology:** 「備え」(sonae = preparation) + 「憂い」(urei = worry) + 「なし」(no)

#### Examples

- 備えあれば憂いなし、準備万端で。 — 事前準備
- 備えあれば憂いなし、防災。 — 防災意識
- 備えあれば憂いなしの精神で。 — 教訓

#### Related Terms

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]] — ことわざ・四字熟語

#### Cultural Notes

防災意識の高い日本社会を反映し、近年特に重要視される表現。

#### Sources

- [[jp-quotes-vocabulary]]

japanese-pop-culture.md.title: 日本のポップカルチャー (Japanese Pop Culture)
japanese-pop-culture.md.body:
# 日本のポップカルチャー (Japanese Pop Culture)

**Overview:** 日本のポップカルチャーは アニメ / 漫画 (manga) / J-POP / ゲーム / 映画 の 5 大ジャンルで構成される 「コンテンツ産業 (contents sangyō)」 として外務省が戦略的に推進。 国内市場規模は約 12 兆円 (2022, コンテンツ産業全体)、 アニメ単独で世界市場シェア 60% を超える。 秋葉原 (Akihabara) が聖地、おたく (otaku) 文化が起源。

## Key Points

- **アニメ (Anime)**: 1958 年の 「鉄腕アトム (Tetsuwan Atom, Astro Boy, 手塚治虫)」 が起源、 1970 年代に 「宇宙戦艦ヤマト」 + 「機動戦士ガンダム」 で黄金期、 1990 年代 「新世紀エヴァンゲリオン (Shin Seiki Evangelion, 1995)」 で再定義。 現在: 「鬼滅の刃 (Kimetsu no Yaiba)」 + 「呪術廻戦 (Jūjutsu Kaisen)」 + 「SPY×FAMILY」 が世界的にヒット。
- **漫画 (Manga)**: 「漫画の神様 (manga no kamisama)」 手塚治虫 (Tezuka Osamu) が現代漫画を体系化。 4 大誌: 「週刊少年ジャンプ (Shūkan Shōnen Jump)」 + 「週刊少年マガジン」 + 「週刊少年サンデー」 + 「月刊コロコロ」 (小学生向け)。 「ONE PIECE (ワンピース)」 は単行本 5 億部+ で世界最多。
- **J-POP**: 1960s グループサウンズ (Group Sounds) → 1970s アイドル (郷ひろみ / ピンク・レディー) → 1980s バンドブーム (BOØWY / X JAPAN) → 1990s J-POP 確立 (B'z / Mr.Children / 安室奈美恵) → 2000s アニメ主題歌 (LiSA / 米津玄師) の流れ。 2020 年代は YOASOBI / Ado / 藤井風 が海外でもヒット。
- **ゲーム (Game) 産業**: 1980 年代 「ファミリーコンピュータ (Family Computer, Famicom, 1983 任天堂)」 が世界市場席巻、 2024 年現在 任天堂 (Nintendo, 京都) + ソニー (Sony, 東京) + バンダイナムコ (Bandai Namco, 東京) の 3 巨頭。 「ポケットモンスター (Pokémon)」 シリーズだけで世界累計 4 億本以上販売。
- **秋葉原 (Akihabara, Tokyo)**: 電気街 (denki-gai) として 1950 年代から電子部品販売、 1990 年代にオタク文化の聖地化。 電気店 + アニメイト + 声優 (seiyū) イベント + 痛車 (itasha) + メイドカフェ (maid café) + ガチャ (gacha, capsule toy) が混在する。 都心から電車で 5 分、新幹線でも 30 分台の 「世界オタク都市」。
- **おたく (Otaku) 文化**: 1983 年に中森明夫 (Nakamori Akio) がコラムで命名、 当初は軽蔑的意味だったが、 2000 年代以降に肯定的に再定義。 2014 年に堺雅人主演ドラマ 「ドラマ 『あまちゃん』」 + アニメ 「アイドルマスター」 の成功でメインストリーム化。

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국은 한류 (한류, Korean Wave) 의 중심이 K-POP + K-Drama + K-Movie + K-Webtoon (WEBTOON). 일본의 만화 와 한국의 웹툰 (webtoon) 은 디지털 시대의 형제. 일본의 秋葉原 와 한국의 홍대 / 신촌 의 오타쿠 거리 가 직접 비교. 韓流 와 ジャパニメーション 의 海外 輸出 은 동시에 진행 — 1990s anime vs 2010s K-pop.
- **Japonés**: 中国은 한난 (漢喃, han-nan) 문화 영향으로 일본의 漢字 표현 그대로 수용. 일본의 「アニメ + 漫画 + ゲーム」 三위 일체 와 중국 의 「小説 + 漫画 + ゲーム」 산업 구조가 거의 동일. 台湾 은 일본의 강력한 콘텐츠 수출 시장.
- **Inglés**: US는 Hollywood + Marvel + DC + Netflix 의 글로벌 플랫폼. 일본의 アニメ 처럼 「アニメ単独で世界市場 60%」 의 지배력은 없음. US의 Comic-Con (サンディエゴ) 은 일본의 「コミケ (Comiket, 東京ビッグサイト)」 와 직접 대응 — 둘 다 fan convention.

## Ejemplos

「秋葉原 (Akihabara) は東京にある電気街で、 アニメ (anime) や 漫画 (manga) 関連のグッズを扱う店、 声優 (seiyū) イベント、 メイドカフェ (maid café) などが集まる場所です。」

「漫画 (manga) 業界では、 手塚治虫 (Tezuka Osamu) が 『鉄腕アトム』 を生み出し、 現代漫画のスタイルを確立しました。 その 後、 『ONE PIECE』 のような世界的にヒットする作品が生まれています。」

「おたく (otaku) 文化は、 アニメや 漫画だけでなく、 J-POP や アイドルにも広がり、 日本国外 (例: フランス / アメリカ) でもファンが急増しています。」

---

japanese-dating-culture.md.title: Japanese Dating Culture
japanese-dating-culture.md.body:
# Japanese Dating Culture

**Type:** 文化ノート, 恋愛
**地域:** 日本 (Japan)

## Overview

일본 데이팅 문화는 **间接(間接)·儀礼(儀礼)·段階(段階)** 중심. 감정 표현은 段階적으로 진행되며, 敬語(경어)에서 タメ口(반말)로의 전환이 관계 진전의 핵심 신호. 告白(고백)은 **공식 이벤트**로, 명확한 의례.

## Setting

A first date in Japan: **カフェ, 動物園, 水族館, 映画, 散歩(산책)**. Often daytime (昼) for first date; evening for established couples. Quiet, conversational activities preferred over loud bars.

## Roles

- **告白する人 (kokuhaku suru hito)** — Confessor (traditionally male, but increasingly either)
- **告白される人 (kokuhaku sareru hito)** — Confessee
- **彼氏 / 彼女 (kareshita / kanojo)** — Boyfriend / girlfriend (after confession)
- **気になる人 (ki ni naru hito)** — "Person of interest" (pre-confession)

## Scenario: Typical First Date → Confession

1. **友達 (Tomodachi)** — Friends, met through school/work/hobby
2. **気になる / 片思い (Ki ni naru / Kataomoi)** — One or both feel attraction
3. **何回かデート (Nankai ka deeto)** — Several dates, group + 1-on-1
4. **告白 (Kokuhaku)** — Confession, often in person, often a "dramatic" moment
5. **付き合う (Tsukiau)** — Officially dating
6. **恋人 (Koibito)** — Established couple

## Cultural Insight

### 告白 (Kokuhaku) 文化

일본에서 告白 = 공식 이벤트. 서양의 "DTR" (Define The Relationship)보다 더 의례적이고 무게감 있음.

**典型的な流れ**:
1. 友達 (친구)
2. 気になる / 片思い (썸/짝사랑)
3. 何回かデート (몇 번 데이트)
4. 告白 (고백, in-person)
5. 付き合う (사귀다)
6. 恋人 (연인)

### 敬語 → タメ口 シフト

**가장 중요한 관계성 전환점**. 연인 사이의 가장 큰 신호 중 하나.

- 그 전: 「○○さん、好きです」
- 후: 「○○ちゃん、好き」

이 시점이 자연스럽게 정해지지 않으면 관계 진행이 막힐 수 있음.

### 脈あり vs 脈なし シグナル

**脈あり (myaku-ari) — 관심이 있는 신호**:
- 자주 연락 (먼저)
- 2人だけの時間 を求める
- ボディタッチ OK (어깨, 팔)
- 食事에 おごろうとする (Z세대: 割り勘 OK)
- 目を見て話す

**脈なし (myaku-nashi) — 관심 없는 신호**:
- 既読スルー (kidoku suru) — LINE 읽고 답장 안 함
- 短返信 (짧은 답장)
- グループに ばかり混ぜようとする
- 視線合わない

### 割り勘 vs おごり

**世代 차이**:
- 30代 이상: 男性 おごり 일반적
- Z世代: 割り勘 (각자 내기) 主流

**판단 기준**: 연인끼리 처음엔 おごり 가능. Z세대는 最初から 割り勘 가능.

### 個人空間 と 距離感

- 初対面: 1m 이상
- 友達: 50cm-1m
- 恋人: 30-50cm (터치 가능)
- 身体接触: 一般的に 서양보다 적음

### 季節と文化

- **クリスマス**: 恋人 일(day). 커플 행위, イルミネーション.
- **バレンタイン (2/14)**: 여성이 남성에게 チョコ. ホワイトデー (3/14): 남성이 답례.
- **お花見 (4월)**: 벚꽃 구경 데이트.
- **夏祭り (8월)**: 전통 축제 데이트.

### 既婚 / 同棲

- 同棲: 점차 보편화 (20-30대)
- 婚前 동거: 一般的

## Useful Phrases

- 好き — I like you
- 綺麗 — beautiful
- 可愛い — cute
- 優しい — kind
- 面白い — interesting/funny
- デート — date
- 告白 — confession
- 付き合う — to date
- 恋人 — lover
- 好きです (suki desu) — I like you
- ありがとう (arigatou) — thank you
- おはよう / おやすみ — good morning / good night (intimacy signal)

## What NOT to Do

- ❌ **ボディタッチ 너무 일찍** — 부담
- ❌ **LINE 너무 자주** — 부담
- ❌ **告白 너무 일찍** — 부담
- ❌ **敬語 → タメ口 너무 늦게** — 관계 막힘
- ❌ **既読スルー 続ける** — 끝
- ❌ **人前で大声で愛情表現** — 매우 부적절
- ❌ **食事のマナー 무시** (음료, 이쑤시개 등) — 일본에서 매우 부정적

## Body Language

| Gesture | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 目を見て話す (eye contact while talking) | 脈あり (interested) |
| 髪を触る (touching hair) | 脈あり (flirting) |
| ボディタッチ (light touch on arm) | 脈あり |
| 足を組む (crossing legs toward you) | 脈あり |
| 腕を組む (crossed arms) | 防御的 / 緊張 |
| 視線を逸らす (looking away) | 緊張 / 脈なし |
| ため口 (casual speech) | 親密 (intimate) — 関係進行中 |

## Cross-Reference

- Compare with: [[english-dating-culture]], [[spanish-dating-culture]], [[korean-dating-culture]]
- See also: 好き, 告白, 付き合う, 恋人

## 一般的な失敗

- **ボディタッチ 너무 일찍** — 부담
- **LINE 너무 자주** — 부담
- **告白 너무 일찍** — 부담
- **敬語 → タメ口 너무 늦게** — 관계 막힘
- **既読スルー 続ける** — 끝

## 例文

「告白」(kokuhaku) は伝統的な恋愛告白の儀式: 通常、好きな相手に直接「好きです」と伝える。
「合コン」(gōkon) はグループでの matchmaking イベントで、男女数人ずつで飲み会をする。
「お見合い」(omiai) は家族や仲介者を通じた正式な出会いの場で、現代でも利用される。

japanese-religious-holidays.md.body:
# 日本の宗教的祝日 (Japanese Religious Holidays)

**Overview:** 日本の祝日は神道 (Shintō, native religion) + 仏教 (bukkyō, Buddhism, 6 世紀伝来) + 儒教 (jukyō, Confucianism) + 民俗 (minkan, folk belief) の四層が複雑に融合した 「年中行事 (nenchū gyōji, annual events)」 を成す。 国民の祝日 (kokumin no shukujitsu) は 16 日 (2024) で、内閣府が制定。

## Key Points

- **お正月 (Oshōgatsu, Jan 1-3)**: 一年で最も重要な行事。 大掃除 (ōsōji, year-end cleaning) → 年越し蕎麦 (toshikoshi soba, NYE noodles) → 除夜の鐘 (joya no kane, 108 temple bells at midnight, 108 = bonno 煩悩 human desires) → 初詣 (hatsumōde, first shrine visit) → おせち料理 (osechi ryōri, stacked celebration foods) + お年玉 (otoshidama, money for children) → 年賀状 (nengajō, New Year's postcards).
- **お盆 (Obon, Aug 13-16)**: 仏教行事、 祖先の霊 (sosen no rei, ancestral spirits) が帰ってくる期間。 迎え火 (mukae-bi) + 送り火 (okuri-bi) で出迎え/見送り。 お盆踊り (Obon odori, folk dance) + 帰省 (kisei, returning home) で大都市は東京が空になる。 沖縄は旧暦 (7 月 15 日)、 京都/関西は 7 月中旬と地域差。
- **ゴールデンウィーク (Gōruden Wīku, late Apr-May)**: 4 連続祝日の総称。 昭和の日 (Shōwa no hi, 4/29) + 憲法記念日 (Kenpō kinenbi, 5/3) + みどりの日 (Midori no hi, 5/4) + こどもの日 (Kodomo no hi, 5/5)。 最大 10 連休、 帰省ラッシュ + 交通渋滞 + 観光地の超混雑。
- **節分 (Setsubun, Feb 3)**: 立春 (risshun, beginning of spring) 前日の豆まき (mamemaki) で邪気 (jaki) を払う。 「鬼は外、 福は内 (Oni wa soto, fuku wa uchi)」 の発声で炒り大豆 (iri daizu) を撒く。 恵方巻き (ehōmaki, lucky direction sushi roll) は 1980 年代以降のコンビニ主導の新伝統。
- **彼岸 (Higan, equinox週)**: 春分の日 (3/20-21) + 秋分の日 (9/22-23) を含む週。 仏教用語の 彼岸 (higan, "this shore" = nirvana, 対岸は shore = enlightenment) で先祖供養 (sosen kuyō)。 ぼた餅 (botamochi, 春) + おはぎ (ohagi, 秋) を食べる習慣。
- **七五三 (Shichi-Go-San, Nov 15)**: 子供の成長祝いの神道行事。 3 歳 (女の子) + 5 歳 (男の子) + 7 歳 (女の子) が神社に参拝、 千歳飴 (chitose ame, long-life candy in red-white bag) + 着物 (kimono) + 記念写真 (kinen shashin, commemorative photo)。 明治改暦前は旧暦 11 月 15 日。

## Cross-language Connections

- **Coreano**: 한국은 설날 (설, lunar Jan 1) + 추석 (秋夕, lunar Aug 15) + 단오 (端午) + 정월대보름 (元宵) 等 음력 (旧暦) 중심. 일본은 양력 (新暦) + 부분 음력 병용. 두 사회 모두 祖上 (조상) 祭祀 가 핵심 (위령제 / 제사) 이지만, 한국은 儒教式 제례 가 더 강함.
- **Japonés**: 中国と共通の 春節 (春節 / 설날) + 盂蘭盆 (중원절) + 七夕 (칠석) + 重陽 (중양절) 의 「四節」 유산. 일본은 二十四節気 (절기) + 旧暦行事 + 新暦行事 의 三層 이 복잡하게 얽힘.
- **Inglés**: US/UK 는 Christmas + Easter + Thanksgiving + Halloween 가 주력. 일본의 お盆 처럼 祖先の霊 을 맞아들이는 행사는 거의 없음 (가톨릭 All Souls Day 정도). US는 Memorial Day / Veterans Day 가 군인 추모이지만, 일반 祖先 의 방문은 없음.

## Ejemplos

「お正月 (Oshōgatsu) には、 家族で初詣 (hatsumōde) に詣でて、 おみくじ (omikuji, fortune slip) を引いたり、 おせち料理 (osechi ryōri) を食べたりします。」

「お盆 (Obon) には、 多くの会社がお休みになり、 都会で仕事をしていた人々は 帰省 (kisei) して、 家族と一緒に先祖の霊 (sosen no rei) を迎えます。」

「七五三 (shichi-go-san) は 11 月 15 日に行われる子供の成長祝いで、 3 歳・5 歳・7 歳の子供が神社 (jinja) にお参りし、 千歳飴 (chitose ame) を受け取ります。」

---
